A transaction-abandonment placement is not required, and it may exist only as the single, time-separated offer after a decline.

summary: Is the analytics client Expo or native Swift?

Describes an Expo client and EAS profiles.
The Expo apps were deleted 2026-07-15.
Native Swift emission.
Native Swift emission.

Defers it to after launch (2026-07-28). No later doc says it shipped.

Marks the same assumptions as unverified.

resolution: Chosen: the unverified reading. Rule 2: the ASO kit banner dated 2026-09-15 retracts its own section 0 and 7 claims as unverified assumptions, and the search-optimization review of the same date lists them one by one. Do not allocate keywords on the 400-character claim.

The local TestFlight recipe or Xcode Cloud.
Xcode Cloud by merge and by tag.

Rule 3: the release flow playbook (restated 2026-09-06) and submission playbook section 11 are newer than the 2026-07-07 setup kit; EAS is not the path. The local recipe's internal eas submit call is a mechanism, not a rule.

.widgets

summary: Is the Family Controls grant account-level, or is one request needed per App ID?

Same claim: account-level grant.
Unproven for new ids; plan one request per App ID.
The question is settled empirically: a signed archive with all extensions exports.
The capability blocked the main app of a new id first.

resolution: Chosen: the capability toggle is enough for a new App ID on this team; file a request only if the toggle is missing. Rule 3: the Lock In Japanese status dated 2026-09-08 (toggle available, no support request needed) is newer than the 2026-09-03 correction that called this unproven.

summary: Does a free rescue pass exist after a paywall decline, or only a paid non-renewing pass?

A paid 30-day pass replaces the automatic free rescue pass; a decline gives no access.
Defines a rescue grant rate guardrail and an automatic grant.

Fix plan: decline -> one offer (Rescue Pass) -> three usable days -> time-separated winback.
A rescue may be a repeatable low-price non-renewing offer; a decline returns to the gate.
A reviewer can reach the core value without a purchase.

resolution: Chosen: no free access after a decline; the one offer is a paid non-renewing pass. Rule 4 and rule 3: the Lock In Chinese review notes for 1.7.12 (2026-09-09) are the newest app fact and agree with the 2026-08-13 rejection fix plan (one offer after a decline). The 2026-08-13 guardrail for an automatic grant is older and stale.

summary: Which bundle id does Lock In Japanese use?

Same example id.
The registered id ends in .ja.

resolution: Chosen: the registered id with the .ja suffix. Rule 4: scripts/asc/apps.json, apps/lockin-japanese/ios/project.yml and the bootstrap status (2026-09-08) hold the fact; the new-app playbook and template give an illustrative example only.

summary: Is a lifetime product required?

It was never wired.
It is an orphan and must not be attached.

resolution: The source retracts itself: the banner on the setup kit says the lifetime product was never wired, and the state file agrees. No requirement asks for a lifetime product. Recorded 2026-09-18 by the seed; an owner may reopen.

summary: Is a 'limited spots' scarcity line allowed?

sides.claim: Includes a scarcity line.
Forbids scarcity lines.

resolution: Chosen: no scarcity line. Rule 6: neither text is dated against the other, so the conservative option wins; the synthesis (section 4 item 5) cites the tactic's own wording and forbids it under the app design law, and a scarcity line cannot cause a rejection when absent.

summary: Does the Lock In Chinese METRICS.md exist?

RevenueCat replaced Adapty.

The table is stale since Sentry and the recorder.

summary: How does a release build start, and what is the TestFlight ship path?

sides.claim: The release workflow starts manually only.
The release workflow starts on a tag.
Start the release workflow by hand, or run the local TestFlight recipe.
Release is by owner-gated tag only; a merge to main is the TestFlight ship.
The UAT loop (fix, tag, TestFlight, user tests) is autonomous; the TestFlight build is a release tag.

resolution: Chosen: a merge to main ships the TestFlight build; a release build starts on an owner-gated tag, with a manual start on the tag ref only when no run appears. Rule 2 and rule 3: the app state file retracts its manual-only text on 2026-07-30, and the release flow playbook (restated 2026-09-06) is the newest statement. The SHIPPING loop wording 'fix, tag, TestFlight' is read with its own rule 2: the tag step is the owner's.

summary: Manual release or release after approval for a launch?

sides.claim: Release is AFTER_APPROVAL.
Use manual release for a first version.
Set release to manual.

resolution: Chosen: manual release for a first version. Rule 4: the playbook (7.9) holds the rule; the app facts table records a pre-action state (AFTER_APPROVAL on 2026-07-28) that the suggested order step 6 tells the owner to change.

Only the 6.9 inch set; read pixel sizes at export time.
6.9 inch only.

Unprefixed key per Wrangler env.
A shared family prefix for the Lock In apps.

Include every subscription in the version's IAP submission set, winback included.

Rule 4: the newest app facts are five renewing subscriptions approved on 2026-09-03 and a sixth non-renewing pass in the 1.7.12 notes (2026-09-09); the three and four counts are older audit states.

A re-run does not repair a partial failure.

Tactic 4 (trial toggle and dual pricing) is CONFORM, shipped 2026-08-01.
Status fixed: toggle removed from both surfaces, three guards.

Agents never tag; only the owner decides.

resolution: Chosen: the decided date 2026-08-01 stands. Rule 2: the growth-ops playbook says 'Ratified 2026-08-01'; the wiki page created 2026-09-04 carried that ratification date. No rule text is in dispute.

summary: A concept page lists experiment evidence against five decided rules. The page states that the decided rules remain unchanged.

sides.claim: Evidence against P-04, P-06, P-07, P-08 and P-10.
All five are decided 2026-09-04.

resolution: Chosen: the decided rules stand. Rule 2 and rule 5: the concept page (2026-09-11) says in its own text that the decided rules remain unchanged and that it is additional evidence, not an owner decision; the wiki says only the owner moves a status.

summary: Minimal first version (P-01) versus longer onboarding (P-08).

sides.claim: First version is minimal.
Longer onboarding wins.

resolution: Chosen: both stand with narrowed scope. Rule 5: P-01 is the specific rule about which parts v1 contains (onboarding is one of the three), and P-08 is about onboarding length; the 'minimal' in P-01 limits the number of parts, not the length of onboarding.

summary: Value moment before the paywall (P-02) versus a hard paywall directly after onboarding (P-06).

sides.claim: Value moment comes before the paywall.
Hard paywall directly after onboarding.

resolution: P-02 reconciles this in its own text: with a hard paywall the value moment sits inside onboarding. The P-02 check uses that reading.

summary: Never copy a paywall (P-05) versus copy a proven format (G-10) versus competitor benchmarks as a gate (P-16). Different surfaces; the registry keeps them as three records.

sides.claim: Forbids one-to-one paywall copies.
Copy a proven content format.
Competitor benchmarks are a gate before changes.

resolution: Chosen: three separate rules. Rule 5: P-05 covers paywalls, G-10 covers content formats, P-16 (candidate) makes benchmarks an input gate; a benchmark is evidence for a derived paywall, not a copy source. P-16 keeps its candidate status because only the owner moves a wiki status.

summary: Discount only the annual plan (P-09) versus a low-price non-renewing rescue offer (P-15, candidate).

sides.claim: Discount only the annual plan.
Allows a low-price non-renewing rescue offer at paywall close.

resolution: Chosen: both stand with narrowed scope. Rule 5: P-09 is specific to the subscription discount on the transaction-abandonment placement; a paywall-close non-renewing pass (P-15) is not a subscription discount. P-15 keeps its candidate status.

summary: Winback never leads with a discount (P-13) versus a price-led rescue offer (P-15). Partial: P-15 limits deeper discounts to cancelled or expired trials.

sides.claim: Winback never leads with a discount.
Introduces a price-led rescue offer.

resolution: Chosen: both stand with narrowed scope. Rule 5: P-13 covers winback after a cancel or expiry; a paywall-close rescue (P-15) is a different surface. Deeper discounts stay bound to cancelled or expired trial evidence, as P-15 itself says. P-15 keeps its candidate status.

summary: Seven verdict cards dated 2026-09-04 cite rules as candidate; the playbook shows the same rules as decided on the same date.

sides.claim: Cite I-, P- and G- rules as (candidate).
The same rules are decided 2026-09-04. Read status only from this page.

resolution: Chosen: read status only from the wiki playbook page. Rule 2: the page says only the owner moves a status and the decision log records the candidate-to-decided move on 2026-09-04; the cards are snapshots taken the same day before that move. The source record for the cards carries this note.
